lessons.title: What is forex?
lessons.subtitle: Buying one, selling another
lessons.body: Forex is the market where currencies are traded against each other, 24 hours a day, five days a week. Every trade is really a pair — you're buying one currency while simultaneously selling another.

lessons.title: Currency pairs
lessons.subtitle: Base currency vs quote currency
lessons.body: A pair like EUR/USD shows how much of the quote currency (USD) it takes to buy one unit of the base currency (EUR). If EUR/USD rises, the euro is strengthening against the dollar.

lessons.title: What is a pip?
lessons.subtitle: The smallest standard price move
lessons.body: The smallest standard price move in a currency pair — usually the 4th decimal place. It's the unit almost everything else (stops, targets, position size) is measured in.

lessons.title: Lot sizes
lessons.subtitle: How trade size is measured
lessons.body: A standard lot is 100,000 units of the base currency. Mini (10,000) and micro (1,000) lots let you scale position size down — useful for controlling risk precisely.

lessons.title: Leverage
lessons.subtitle: Trading with borrowed exposure
lessons.body: Leverage lets you control a large position with a small deposit (margin). It multiplies gains — and losses — equally, which is why sizing and stops matter more as leverage increases.

lessons.title: Bid, ask & spread
lessons.subtitle: The cost built into every trade
lessons.body: The bid is what you can sell at, the ask is what you can buy at. The gap between them — the spread — is effectively the cost of entering a trade before it moves in your favor.

lessons.title: Long vs short
lessons.subtitle: Profiting from rises or falls
lessons.body: Buying (long) profits if the pair rises. Selling (short) profits if it falls. In forex you can do either just as easily — there's no extra step to "short" a currency.

lessons.title: Support & resistance
lessons.subtitle: Where price tends to react
lessons.body: Price levels where buying or selling pressure has repeatedly shown up in the past. They're not exact lines — think of them as zones where reactions become more likely.

lessons.title: Trend vs range
lessons.subtitle: Going somewhere, or nowhere?
lessons.body: A trending market makes higher highs and higher lows (or the reverse). A ranging market oscillates between a ceiling and a floor. Different conditions call for different approaches.

lessons.title: Reading candlesticks
lessons.subtitle: Open, high, low, close at a glance
lessons.body: Each candle shows four prices for a period: open, high, low and close. The body shows the open-to-close range; the wicks show how far price reached beyond that before pulling back.

lessons.title: Position sizing
lessons.subtitle: Size trades by risk, not confidence
lessons.body: How much you trade should be set by how much you're willing to lose, not by how confident you feel. Fix your risk per trade first, then work backward to the position size.

lessons.title: Risk:reward ratio
lessons.subtitle: What you risk vs what you stand to gain
lessons.body: Compares what you stand to lose (distance to your stop) against what you stand to gain (distance to your target). A positive edge times a good ratio is what makes a strategy worth repeating.

lessons.title: Stop loss & take profit
lessons.subtitle: Deciding your exit before you enter
lessons.body: A stop loss caps what a trade can cost you if it goes wrong; a take profit locks in a target if it goes right. Setting both before entering removes emotion from the exit.

lessons.title: Why "no trade" is a decision
lessons.subtitle: Skipping a setup is still a skill
lessons.body: Every setup you see isn't automatically worth acting on. Skilled traders pass on far more setups than they take — recognizing when not to act is a skill in itself.

lessons.title: Correlation between pairs
lessons.subtitle: Some pairs move together
lessons.body: Pairs that share a currency, like EUR/USD and GBP/USD, often move in similar directions. Trading several correlated pairs at once can multiply risk without you realizing it.

lessons.title: Trading sessions
lessons.subtitle: Volatility changes by time of day
lessons.body: The forex day is split into Asian, London and New York sessions. Volatility and spreads shift as sessions open, overlap and close — worth knowing before you set a stop.
